title: Boss: chain detective
summary: Sort certificates into a chain, classify them, and find the missing link.

steps.title: The case
body: A partner's server sends you a pile of certificates in no particular order. Your job: make sense of the pile.
Every test certificate is valid from 2030 to 2035 and carries Basic Constraints, a Subject Key Identifier and, when issued
by a CA, an Authority Key Identifier. The namespaces are imported.

steps.title: Who's who
prompt: Write `string Role(X509Certificate2 cert)` that returns:
- `"root"` when the certificate is self-signed (Subject equals Issuer) and is a CA,
- `"intermediate"` when it is a CA but not self-signed,
- `"leaf"` otherwise (Basic Constraints says not a CA, or is missing).
hints: Decide CA or not first, using `X509BasicConstraintsExtension`.
For a CA, compare Subject and Issuer.
template: var dojoRoot = DojoCert("CN=Dojo Root", null, true);
var dojoInter = DojoCert("CN=Dojo Issuing CA", dojoRoot, true);
Dojo.Eq("a self-signed dev cert that is not a CA is a leaf", "leaf", Role(dojoDev));
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);

steps.title: Sort the pile
prompt: Write `List<X509Certificate2> SortChain(List<X509Certificate2> pile)` that returns the certificates in chain order,
leaf first. The pile contains exactly one chain, possibly with the root and possibly without.
The leaf is the certificate that is not the issuer of any other certificate in the pile
(no other certificate's `Issuer` equals its `Subject`). From there, follow `Issuer` to `Subject` as before.
solution: var current = pile.First(c => !pile.Any(o => o != c && o.Issuer == c.Subject));
hints: Find the leaf: `pile.First(c => !pile.Any(o => o != c && o.Issuer == c.Subject))`. The `o != c` matters for a self-signed root.
Then loop: add, stop at self-signed, otherwise find the certificate whose Subject is the current Issuer.
template: var dojoRoot = DojoCert("CN=Dojo Root", null, true);
var dojoPolicy = DojoCert("CN=Dojo Policy CA", dojoRoot, true);
var dojoIssuing = DojoCert("CN=Dojo Issuing CA", dojoPolicy, true);
Dojo.Eq("four certificates, shuffled", new List<string> { "CN=shop.example", "CN=Dojo Issuing CA", "CN=Dojo Policy CA", "CN=Dojo Root" },
DojoNames(SortChain(new List<X509Certificate2> { dojoPolicy, dojoRoot, dojoLeaf, dojoIssuing })));
Dojo.Eq("no root in the pile", new List<string> { "CN=shop.example", "CN=Dojo Issuing CA", "CN=Dojo Policy CA" },
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);

steps.title: The missing link
prompt: A chain breaks when some certificate's issuer can't be found. Write
`string MissingIssuer(X509Certificate2 leaf, List<X509Certificate2> sent, List<X509Certificate2> trusted)` that walks
up from `leaf`, looking for each issuer by **Subject name** among `sent` and `trusted` together, and returns:
- `""` (empty) if the walk reaches a certificate that is in `trusted` (compare `Thumbprint`s),
- otherwise the **Issuer name** that could not be found.
```text
leaf -> (Issuing CA not sent) ...   returns "CN=Dojo Issuing CA"
A self-signed certificate that is not trusted counts as missing its trusted issuer: return its own Issuer name.
starter: string MissingIssuer(X509Certificate2 leaf, List<X509Certificate2> sent, List<X509Certificate2> trusted)
solution: string MissingIssuer(X509Certificate2 leaf, List<X509Certificate2> sent, List<X509Certificate2> trusted)
hints: Check "is current trusted?" at the top of each loop step.
Handle the self-signed case before looking for a parent, or you'll loop forever on an untrusted root.
template: var dojoRoot = DojoCert("CN=Dojo Root", null, true);
var dojoInter = DojoCert("CN=Dojo Issuing CA", dojoRoot, true);
Dojo.Eq("complete chain", "", MissingIssuer(dojoLeaf, new List<X509Certificate2> { dojoInter }, new List<X509Certificate2> { dojoRoot }));
Dojo.Eq("intermediate not sent", "CN=Dojo Issuing CA", MissingIssuer(dojoLeaf, dojoNone, new List<X509Certificate2> { dojoRoot }));
Dojo.Eq("root not trusted (server sent it, we don't trust it)", "CN=Dojo Root", MissingIssuer(dojoLeaf, new List<X509Certificate2> { dojoInter, dojoRoot }, dojoNone));
Dojo.Eq("root not trusted and not sent", "CN=Dojo Root", MissingIssuer(dojoLeaf, new List<X509Certificate2> { dojoInter }, dojoNone));
Dojo.Eq("the intermediate itself is trusted", "", MissingIssuer(dojoLeaf, dojoNone, new List<X509Certificate2> { dojoInter }));
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);
steps.explain: The last case is real: a trust store can hold an intermediate as an anchor. The walk stops at the first trusted certificate, wherever it is.

steps.title: Let .NET do it
prompt: Now use the real chain engine. Write `List<string> ChainSubjects(X509Certificate2 leaf, List<X509Certificate2> sent, X509Certificate2 root)`
that builds an `X509Chain` (custom root trust with `root`, `sent` in `ExtraStore`, no revocation,
`VerificationTime` 2031-06-01 UTC) and returns:
- the `Subject` of every element in `chain.ChainElements`, leaf first, when `Build` succeeds,
- an **empty list** when it fails.
starter: List<string> ChainSubjects(X509Certificate2 leaf, List<X509Certificate2> sent, X509Certificate2 root)
solution: List<string> ChainSubjects(X509Certificate2 leaf, List<X509Certificate2> sent, X509Certificate2 root)
hints: Reuse your `Validates` setup from the trust-stores lesson.
template: var dojoRoot = DojoCert("CN=Dojo Root", null, true);
var dojoInter = DojoCert("CN=Dojo Issuing CA", dojoRoot, true);
var dojoDecoy = DojoCert("CN=Decoy CA", dojoRoot, true);
Dojo.Eq("full chain, with a decoy in the pile", new List<string> { "CN=shop.example", "CN=Dojo Issuing CA", "CN=Dojo Root" },
ChainSubjects(dojoLeaf, new List<X509Certificate2> { dojoDecoy, dojoInter }, dojoRoot));
Dojo.Eq("missing intermediate gives an empty list", new List<string>(), ChainSubjects(dojoLeaf, new List<X509Certificate2> { dojoDecoy }, dojoRoot));
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);
